memo.verdict: Progress Airtel Africa (AAF-GB) to Early-Stage Assessment, medium conviction, rather than park. Trigger conditions before the case can carry more weight: confirm the exact country/business-unit perimeter (via the Business Foundations report), quantify diesel and foreign-exchange sensitivity to the P&L (the disclosed $29m-$31m per-1%-move EBITDA base), and track the delayed Airtel Money IPO toward its revised H2-2026 target. Why not park: no Element in the memo grades [F] at the headline level, and the Triaging qualitative test (large amounts of positive change forces) is clearly met on data and mobile-money evidence. Why only medium not high conviction: Element E7 fails on 4 of 5 Required Attributes and the Element E1 robust-base test fails on 2 of 5 Core Questions, both genuine rather than marginal caveats. Reached with zero bespoke research queries, per Triaging stage discipline.
case: Overall case [C]: the change thesis is real, quantified and multi-sourced. Internal change forces: near-simultaneous planned replacement of CEO, CFO and board chair inside a 24-month window, anchored by Bharti insiders for continuity, plus a deliberate digital-first, asset-light pivot with mobile-money separation. External change forces: data usage per subscriber up 37.0% y/y to 9.8GB/month; Sub-Saharan mobile internet penetration at only 27% offers a multi-decade growth runway; Nigerian regulator approved tariff increases of up to 50% in early 2025. Delivery has repeatedly tracked ahead of consensus: Q4 revenue $1,748m and EBITDA $879m both beat by ~4.0%; Q3 revenue beat by 4.1% and EBITDA by 5.0% — a repeated, not one-off, pattern. The base is well-invested (capex +31.9% to $884m, FY27 guidance raised to $1.1bn) and shows delivery congruency with the thesis. Element E8 finds two positive setup fits: primary fit under strong corporate-change-driven EPS upgrade/earnings-power turn (leadership reset, dividend +9.2%, new buyback, mobile-money perimeter reduction, digital-first strategy change — 5 of 9 CQs positively evidenced [B]); secondary fit under big-demand change-driven upgrade (structurally accelerating data/mobile-money demand, 280bps margin expansion evidencing operating leverage, oligopoly market structure with high entry barriers). Element E11 (Value-chain dynamics, [C]) is carried by demand-side strength: data usage growth and a 54.1m mobile-money customer base (+21.3%) evidence a large, growing route to market. Cohort-anchored: change-forces evidence is unusually well quantified versus TCM08 peers, closer to Deutsche Telekom's multi-driver momentum than to 4iG's narrative-heavier six-driver case. Guidance credibility (E7.RA5, [B]) is the single strongest Required Attribute across both E7 and E1 — capex landed exactly within the $875m-$900m guidance band. No Element in the memo grades [F] at the headline level, and the Triaging qualitative test is clearly met.
counter_case: The base the change forces sit on is not robust and the case fails the simplicity guardrail outright. Element E1's Required Attribute 2 (Robust base, [D]) fails the absence-of-headwinds and low-multiple tests: diesel generators fund 30-40% of network operating costs, a direct commodity-price exposure, and management has explicitly guided 250-300bps of possible FY27 EBITDA margin compression from sustained high fuel prices; the 234% naira devaluation (NGN 461 to NGN 1,542/USD) already suppressed reported USD earnings once and could recur. The 13.8x forward multiple sits at the 99th percentile of the stock's own ten-year range — near the richest it has ever traded — materially different from a genuinely cheap entry point, and three consecutive Deutsche Bank target upgrades (390p→430p→450p) suggest the market has already been progressively re-rating the shares. Element E7 (Required case simplicity guardrails, [D]) fails four of five Required Attributes: the case runs on five named key drivers (structural data penetration, mobile-money expansion, cost-efficiency execution, FX stabilisation, accelerated capex) against a four-driver ceiling, with no fulcrum-driver tiering supplied; the confirmed footprint spans Nigeria, East Africa and Francophone operations across distinct currency/regulatory regimes (Required Attribute 3, Zero headwinds, fails at [F] — the most load-bearing failure in the Element); multiple concurrent change-from-current items (CEO/CFO/chair change, mobile-money carve-out, asset-light pivot) raise genuine execution risk. Element E5 (Thematic fit, [D]): the business sits outside the current risk-off, domestic-EU-defensive frame Richard favours; Required Attribute 3 (Iran oil-price transmission) carries the most decision-relevant, quantified evidence of the four Required Attributes and is the primary reason the Element grades [D] rather than [C]. Element E8's false-friend caution (Required Attribute 8, [C]): the $127m full-year FX derivative gain sharply reverses prior-year losses and flatters the reported EPS doubling; the 50.3% group margin still trails MTN Nigeria's 55.3%; two of the five covering analysts model Airtel Africa only through consolidated parent Bharti Airtel metrics. Competitively, MTN leads Nigeria with 52.4% share against Airtel's 33.9%, a persistent rather than closing gap, in the largest single market. A cross-element tension is flagged as a first-order item for Early-Stage Assessment, not a footnote: a genuine setups fit under Element E8 sits awkwardly alongside a simplicity guardrail failing on four of five Required Attributes. The memo records no separate named Risks-report recommendation; the base-and-simplicity caveats above are carried within the memo's own analysis as the reason conviction is medium rather than high.
triggers: Four questions anchor Early-Stage Assessment, in priority order: (1) Does the exact geography/business-unit count confirm or overturn the directional narrow-perimeter fail under Element E7? (2) How does quantified diesel/naira sensitivity compare against the disclosed 250-300bps FY27 margin-risk guidance? (3) Does the confirmed CEO successor strengthen or weaken the primary corporate-change setup under Element E8? (4) Has the margin gap to MTN Nigeria (50.3% vs 55.3%) narrowed or widened by the next reporting period, testing the false-friend caution under Element E8? Immediate downstream actions: Watson to brief the Chief of Staff to prioritise the Business Foundations report read at Early-Stage Assessment pickup (perimeter/geography gap); Watson to build a diesel-price and naira-sensitivity table anchored on the $29m-$31m per-1%-move EBITDA sensitivity, feeding Element E1, E5 and E11 from one source. What would raise conviction to high: confirmation the perimeter is narrower than the current multi-currency footprint suggests, or a materially narrowed margin gap to MTN Nigeria. What would lower conviction toward park: a further naira devaluation reversing the disclosed FX derivative gain, or a second delay to the Airtel Money listing beyond H2-2026. Element-specific watch-lists: named CEO successor and any strategy restatement (E1, E8); whether the canonical thematics file is refreshed beyond its lapsed Q2-2026 period, and whether diesel prices continue rising through the Iran-conflict period (E5); fulcrum-driver tiering among the five key drivers, and exact country/business-unit perimeter (E7); updated Nigeria competitive-share data, diesel-contract/hedging structure, and confirmation of fintech/OTT adjacent-competition evidence (E11). Two judgement calls flagged for Richard personally: whether a genuinely strong operating business outside the current domestic-EU defensive paradigm warrants continued pipeline time given his risk-off positioning; whether the thin five-broker/five-analyst coverage pool (two of five modelling only through the parent) is an acceptable evidentiary base for a position of meaningful size.
